Read; 2 L.
High Jump.—1 L.
We have been glad to welcome Les Christmas, who joined us during the winter. He has shown quite good form in both the Long Jump and Hop Step and Jump.
We had a club 220 yards handicap event on the same programme and this was won by Les Christmas (18), with Jim Heathfield (14), on leave from the B.A.O.R., second and Charlie Jones (20) third.
Les Christmas ran in the 100 yards and did well to gain second place, while for the next event the 880 yards, we had Ben Lulham and Freddie Bradnum, and Lulham gained second place in a slow run race.
Wood (7); 2 L.
Held at Tooting on July 14th, and once again we were poorly represented in the sprint events, although Les Christmas did well in gaining third place in both races.
Heat 3—1, L.
Broadbent 2; L.

"Steve" Gibson, Les Christmas and Stan Botwright will be our main hopes in the Long Jump, but it would be good to see Geoff Wood taking part in this event more often as it is felt he has good possibilities.
They also did well in the short sprints with Lewis scoring a double and our only placed man in these events was Les Christmas, third in the 220.
Barker second (39 ft. 6 ins), and L.

Lowers beat Basil Walden for the first place and in the 220 yards Paddy Mullen beat Les Christmas in 23.5 secs. Len Marchant won the 880 yards in 1 min. 59.4 secs. and then turned out in the 2 miles to record another win in 9 mins. 58 secs.

In the Long Jump and Hop, Step and Jump, Les Christmas is again available, and we hope will show improvement. Now that Pete Lowe has recovered from his injury we look forward to having him in both these events.
220 yards Hurdles.—1, L.
As usual we were minus any high jumpers, but Les Christmas and our new member, Odde, very sportingly filled in, in order to score points for the third and fourth places.
We had a new innovation with a 120 Yards Low Hurdles handicap, and John Briggs the scratch man was just beaten by Les Christmas with Peter Hunt in third place.
Lowe, 40 ft. 7½ ins.; 3, L.
